## Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

We have presented the Epoch Merkle Log, a verifiable append-only data
structure that addresses the upgrade trilemma for hash algorithm
transitions in verifiable logs. By partitioning algorithm lifecycles
into null-padded chronological epochs over a shared RFC 9162 topology,
the EML achieves $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ algorithm addition with zero
retroactive computation, strictly algorithm-independent verification via
the projection equivalence, and zero per-proof-metadata compression through
deterministic elision. Historical data remains bound to the algorithms
active at the time of insertion---a principled trade-off that preserves
temporal fidelity while eliminating operational fragmentation.

The formal model (13 definitions and 5 theorems, machine-checked in Lean 4)
reduces multi-algorithm correctness to the well-understood correctness of
single-algorithm RFC 9162 verification. The production Rust
implementation validates these properties empirically through
property-based testing, fault injection, complexity regression, and
sustained fuzz testing.

Epoch boundaries transform what has historically been a global
infrastructure crisis---coordinating hash algorithm deprecation across
distributed systems---into a locally managed, formally verifiable
structural operation. A log operator adds a post-quantum hash algorithm
in $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ time. The cryptographic verification core
remains standard RFC 9162: clients receiving unelided proofs verify
without modification. Elision-aware clients perform a rehydration step
before invoking the same verification core, requiring no degradation in
the security of their own algorithm's verification.

### Future Work

- **Post-quantum hash integration.** Integrating the EML with Merkle
  Tree Certificates [@mtc-draft] would combine per-epoch hash lifecycle
  management with amortized post-quantum signature costs.

- **P2P replication semantics.** The EML's append-only guarantees and
  per-algorithm consistency proofs are natural building blocks for
  gossip-based log replication, but the replication protocol is an
  application-layer concern outside the scope of this work.

- **STH signature agility.** The EML specifies the STH payload
  structure (Definition 8) but does not address signature agility for
  the signing key $\sigma$. The manifest commitment is independent of the signature
  scheme used to authenticate the tree head payload, ensuring that extending
  the epoch lifecycle model to asymmetric key rotation can be executed cleanly
  at the transport layer without altering the underlying tree algebra.
